A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same HARP study and contain 26 readable pages, including Appendices A-D. Text, equations, tables, and figures can be matched reliably despite page reflow.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark evaluations, layer-selection and rescaling ablations, and inference timing measurements (Tables 2-6; Figure 3).

after.justification: v3 retains the same original benchmark, ablation, and timing results (Tables 2-6; Figure 3).

M1.justification: Section 2.3 and Algorithm 1 retain identical high-layer query/key pruning, value/output projections, rescaling, and top-down parameter search procedures.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same generation and discriminative benchmarks, 16 LongBench datasets, and WikiText/Pile10K calibration checks (Section 3; Appendix C).

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains identical within corresponding experiments, including Mag-sp, Wanda-sp, FLAP, and LLM-Pruner where originally evaluated. Dense-model and HARP+FLAP comparisons are also retained.

E3.justification: Model configurations, pruning ratios, few-shot settings, scoring metrics, baseline layer-range tuning, and timing-test sequence lengths remain unchanged (Section 3; Appendices B-C).

E4.justification: The layer-selection comparisons, rescaling ablation, calibration-dataset sensitivity checks, and searched rescaling profiles are identical (Sections 3.4-3.5; Tables 5-6; Figure 2).

E5.justification: Section 3.6 reports the same 10 repetitions and 95% confidence intervals for timing measurements in both versions. No statistical reporting practices are added or removed.

E6.justification: Benchmark, ablation, calibration, and timing results match throughout. For example, Table 2 retains HARP's 31.10 generation average on LLaMA3.1-8B, and Section 3.6 retains the reported 16.7% speed improvement.

T1.justification: The complexity analysis, definitions, Theorem 1, Proposition 1, Appendix A lemmas and proofs, and Appendix D heuristic formulas are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contribution: training-free high-layer attention pruning with rescaling, together with the same comparative performance and efficiency claims.

C2.justification: Explanations of high-layer redundancy, rescaling, task sensitivity, and search overhead are retained. The conclusion preserves the same limitations and proposed extensions to other components, larger models, and multimodal models.

D1.justification: Implementation links, evaluation-harness version 0.4.7, H100 hardware, search settings and runtime, and technical details in Appendices B-D remain identical.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works, bibliography, and positioning relative to prior research are unchanged. Reference entries merely flow onto different pages.

P1.justification: v3 removes the repeated TMLR publication header and first-page OpenReview review notice/link, and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Scientific prose and section structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Notice removal changes first-page spacing and subsequent paragraph and reference page breaks. Algorithm 1, Tables 1-8, and Figures 1-3 retain their content, structure, captions, and numbering.

improvement.justification: The changes concern publication/review notices and page layout. The scientific argument, experiments, results, proofs, limitations, and reproducibility information remain identical, including the appendices. These edits establish no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
